requirements.title: AI transfer and declaration procedure
requirements.summary: Current Engineering students, including first- and second-year M&T students, may apply by submitting a four-year academic plan and the Declare/Update Field of Study form. Other students must satisfy the separate Engineering transfer-in eligibility rules.

requirements.title: Graduation limit for changing into AI
requirements.summary: The major change is not approved unless graduation remains possible within eight total semesters, or ten for M&T students.

requirements.title: Dual majors and other degrees
requirements.summary: Engineering dual majors are permitted except CSCI, NETS and SSE. Eligibility for dual degrees or College of Arts and Sciences second majors, including VIPER, requires program advising review.

requirements.title: Incoming M&T declaration timing
requirements.summary: Incoming first-year M&T students may begin declaring AI on the first day of their first fall semester using the field-of-study form.

requirements.title: Scope of the linked technical-elective list
requirements.summary: The CIS handbook explicitly allows its approved technical-elective entries in ARIN. Its subsequent restricted-course quotas concern the 37-CU CSCI degree and are not applied here. The AI program separately permits Engineering, Mathematics and Natural Science courses.

requirements.title: Technical electives requiring individual approval
requirements.summary: These entries are marked ask and are not included as automatically approved options. Seek the CIS undergraduate chair’s decision with supporting documentation before counting one.

requirements.title: Applicable curriculum and major changes
requirements.summary: Use the curriculum associated with the Penn entering catalog year. Major changes require the field-of-study form and meetings with the current advisor and receiving program chair.

requirements.title: Credit away and transfer residence
requirements.summary: Credit away is limited to four course units for students entering Fall 2020 or later, requires prior department approval, and is summer-only with at least C. Penn summer plus credit away cannot exceed four units per summer. Two-year-institution, high-school-era, leave-of-absence and academic-drop coursework is excluded. External transfer students must complete at least half their graduation courses at Penn; those transferring five or more courses cannot take further credit away. Failed Penn courses cannot be cleared elsewhere. Approved study abroad and the Quaker Consortium have separate policies.

requirements.title: Engineering dual-major rules
requirements.summary: ARIN cannot dual major with ASCS, CSCI, NETS or SSE. An allowed Engineering dual major must satisfy both curricula and at least 22 Engineering courses, with at most one 1000-level course outside the two majors. One senior-design project suffices; use the larger unit requirement when they differ. Apply with an approved academic plan by the start of junior year or 20 relevant units. Generally a 3.0 cumulative GPA is required. No course may count toward more than two degrees/majors.

requirements.title: Engineering ethics: source discrepancy
requirements.summary: The handbook permits EAS 2030 for Engineering ethics and permits overlap with SS/H/TBS, without extra degree units. It limits CIS 4230/5230 ethics eligibility to a named list that omits ARIN, although the AI program lists CIS 4230 in its own ethics pool. Preserve this unresolved program/college discrepancy rather than silently overriding either source. VIPER has separate VIPR 1200/1210 permission and those courses cannot be SS/H.

requirements.title: Uncleared grades and incomplete work
requirements.summary: Graduation requires clearing F/U, I and NR entries. Failed courses require repetition or an approved substitution; failures remain in the cumulative GPA. Starting Summer 2026, incomplete work in undergraduate Engineering courses must be completed by the following enrolled semester’s grade-mode deadline; the instructor must submit the change by that deadline or the converted F becomes permanent. Earlier I/NR conversion deadlines and any exceptions remain governed by the handbook.

requirements.title: Minimum academic performance
requirements.summary: Maintain cumulative GPA of at least 2.0 and at least 2.0 across all mathematics, science and Engineering courses. Academic progress means averaging at least eight successfully completed course units each academic year.

requirements.title: Pass/fail limits
requirements.summary: At most four degree course units may be pass/fail, normally one course per term, and only in SS/H/TBS/free-elective categories. Additional pass/fail is possible for courses beyond the degree minimum; overload exceptions need a petition. D or better earns P without GPA weight, while F counts. A failed pass/fail course cannot be repeated pass/fail. Grade-mode changes must meet the ninth-week or pre-registration deadline, whichever comes first; writing changes require the registrar procedure.

requirements.title: Repeated courses
requirements.summary: Do not repeat a passed course (D or better), or take a course substantially repeating earlier material; related later courses should have higher-level content.

requirements.title: Humanities/social science breadth applicability
requirements.summary: The handbook’s two-social-science/two-humanities breadth rule is explicitly retained for 40-unit curricula and waived for some others. The AI degree lists 37 units; its exact breadth applicability needs department confirmation. The department-based SS/H classifications and exceptions are not yet fully enumerated here.

requirements.title: Humanities/social science depth scope
requirements.summary: The handbook’s specific SSH depth rule applies only to 40-unit Engineering curricula. Do not impose it as an additional requirement on the 37-unit AI curriculum.

requirements.title: Maximum elapsed degree time
requirements.summary: Complete the BAS/BSE within eight calendar years after matriculation. An extension requires a petition and review that may impose additional or replacement coursework. This differs from the AI major-change limit measured in semesters.

requirements.title: Internal Engineering transfer eligibility
requirements.summary: Internal applicants need a four-year plan naming the intended major, eight completed Penn units, at least 3.0 GPA and no uncleared F/I/GR/NR. Calculus preparation and normally physics are reviewed by major and semesters completed. Students who entered Penn as external transfers cannot use this internal-transfer route. Apply before sophomore year ends; the published fall/spring entry deadlines are May 15 and December 15. Application availability is separate from eligibility.

requirements.title: Writing policy and grade mode
requirements.summary: Complete a critical writing seminar, preferably in year one and no later than year two. AP credit cannot satisfy writing. Writing may be pass/fail through the registrar process by the drop deadline, but dual-degree students must take it for a grade. WRIT classification determines its distribution slot; a free-elective classification does not automatically qualify within the AI program’s five-unit SS/H distribution.

requirements.title: Social Science and Humanities Courses Requirement
requirements.summary: SS/H excludes business and military-science subjects, primarily mathematical/physical-science courses and primarily skill-training courses, except explicit classified exceptions. Up to two SS/H courses may be substituted with approved TBS courses, subject to the unresolved AI breadth applicability rule. WRIT follows its individual classification.

requirements.title: Technology in Business and Society Courses
requirements.summary: At most two approved TBS courses may substitute for SS/H. New unlisted options need OAS/undergraduate-chair review before enrollment. TBS cannot also be classified as Engineering. The TBS page reiterates two SS plus two H and depth/writing; applicability to 37-CU ARIN remains unresolved. EAS2420 ceased qualifying in Spring2025. OIDD2340 is M&T-only; OIDD3990 plus WH1010 combine to one TBS CU for M&T. EAS5050 appears here but is also on the no-credit list: do not resolve that conflict by silently permitting it.

requirements.summary: PFP Free: (approved for entered Fall 2020 and later)

requirements.title: Course Load
requirements.summary: Normal enrollment is five courses; below4CU or above5.5CU needs advisor sign-off. First-term maximum is5.5CU. Later overloads need good standing,3.0GPA,no incompletes and a per-term request before add deadline;7CU needs a petition and plan. Probation maximum is4.5CU. Summer limits are4CU over11weeks and2CU per short session. These are enrollment rules, not extra degree credits.

requirements.title: Graduate-level Courses
requirements.summary: Some5000-level courses need advisor/instructor approval;6000+ needs the course-permission form;7000-level also needs graduate-chair and associate-dean signatures. At least half enrolled CUs each term should satisfy the undergraduate degree, and no more than half should be graduate-level. Exceeding the graduate share affects undergraduate financial-aid eligibility.

requirements.title: Independent Study
requirements.summary: Independent study needs a standing-faculty supervisor and application by the add deadline; maximum2CU within the undergraduate degree. Internship-based credit must produce an academic product; approved0099 enrollment is1CU graded, not pass/fail. Students must be actively in an Engineering degree/major.

requirements.title: Petition for Action
requirements.summary: Requirement deviations need Petition for Action review; engineering/technical elective substitutions also need the departmental Core Sub Form. Degree-rule exceptions go to the affected school(s); other enrollment petitions go to the home school. Final decisions rest with the Petitions Committee.

requirements.title: Quaker Consortium
requirements.summary: Penn Engineering students may take Bryn Mawr, Haverford or Swarthmore courses in fall/spring through the Quaker Consortium. Grades enter the Penn transcript under the reciprocal credit arrangement. The linked registration instructions require login; no portal was accessed.

requirements.title: Advanced Placement
requirements.summary: Taking the Penn equivalent forfeits corresponding AP credit. Chemistry lecture AP does not itself supply lab credit; an approved lab-experience waiver removes the lab requirement but supplies no credits. Subject exam/placement equivalencies require the registrar and relevant department; no new blanket ARIN substitution is inferred.

requirements.title: Approved study-abroad eligibility
requirements.summary: Require good academic/disciplinary standing,3.0 cumulative and prior-term GPA,no prior-term failures/GR,and a plan to resolve I/NR before departure. At least7CU must remain. First-year students and seniors are ineligible for semester abroad; the earliest abroad period is summer after year one. Program approval and advisor sign-off are required.

requirements.title: Study-abroad course approval
requirements.summary: Plan with advisors to finish in eight semesters without forced overload. All abroad courses require XCAT approval and posting; submit a final course list and official return transcript. Courses numbered2980 need a core-substitution request. Penn determines credit equivalence and appropriate requirement slots; approved-program availability is not individual approval.

requirements.title: Study-abroad load and grades
requirements.summary: Normally take4–4.5 Penn-equivalent CU. Host-required higher loads and qualifying dual degrees have exceptions; the XCAT section permits up to5.5CU for dual degrees. All abroad courses must appear on the Penn transcript, and grades enter the cumulative GPA. Pass/fail remains subject to Engineering policy and notice to the abroad advisor by5PM ET Friday of the ninth program week.

notes: The program webpage is undated and is not assigned a catalog year. The catalog URL returned an empty response; program-page evidence supports the record.

The overview says students choose a concentration, but the explicit AI Concentrations section says concentrations are optional and use four of the six AI elective courses. This inconsistency is unresolved.
Course options may appear in several categories. Listed pools must not be summed; this record does not assert double-counting permission.

They are analyst classifications, not institution-stated learning outcomes or guarantees that every student completes every theme. Source-stated outcomes are retained separately.

Linked approved lists, college-wide completion rules, and the overview/concentration inconsistency remain unresolved; degree curriculum stays partial. Individual course metadata are separate and are not inferred from section totals.

Optional pool membership does not automatically authorize use outside the AI Elective category. Transfer timing and dual-major restrictions in the FAQ require further structured review.

STAT 4300 title was verified through the official technical-elective inventory; individual units and prerequisites remain unknown.

The old ugrad.seas.upenn.edu robots URL redirected to the current academic-services landing page, not a robots policy; this was a migration/review condition, not a demonstrated publisher denial. The canonical host has a valid robots policy and its handbook was subsequently inspected.

Current canonical handbook policies and 49 writing classifications are mapped. General depth applies only to 40-unit curricula and is not imposed on the 37-unit AI degree. AI-specific ethics/breadth ambiguities remain visible instead of silently combining inconsistent rules.

All visible college natural-science, mathematics, SS/H, TBS, Engineering and no-credit classification rules are now mapped. They classify potential options; they do not override ARIN requirements or impose all pool courses.

Handbook source numbering includes legacy codes and cohort/major-specific conditions. They are retained as factual policy notes without guessing modern equivalents or extending another program’s exceptions to ARIN. Names are null for code-only classification entries.
TBS lists EAS5050 while the no-credit list excludes it; preserve this additional source conflict. College ethics,37CU breadth and optional-concentration conflicts remain unresolved.

Study-abroad and Consortium permission rules are represented from public sources. XCAT and student-specific approvals were not accessed or fabricated; no individually approved substitution or graduation clearance is implied.

CIS 4190/5190 identifies Fall 2026 and CIS 5210 Summer 2026; CIS 4210 Fall 2022 and CIS 5200 Spring 2023 are historical examples, with current prerequisite fields left unknown. unresolved_requirements: The AI ethics pool and generic Engineering ethics course-eligibility list are not reconciled; the latter omits ARIN from CIS 4230/5230 eligibility.
Breadth applicability for the 37-unit AI curriculum requires department clarification; the handbook explicitly scopes its depth rule to 40-unit curricula.
EAS 5050 appears in the TBS approved list but also in the Engineering degree no-credit list; authoritative eligibility for ARIN is unresolved.
